svg.aria-label: Wrapping paper artwork rules: the repeat tile butts cleanly on all four sides, motifs sit on an angle, small type stays out of the tile, with quarter-inch bleed beyond trim

g.text: The repeat tile is the artwork's contract
Any fold should show the brand, not a blank gap or a broken seam — the tile rules decide that before anything prints
trim line
bleed — quarter-inch beyond trim (StationeryHQ: 20.25×29.25 for a finished 20×29 sheet)
every edge is a trim edge
Tile rules that survive the fold
1 · Butt cleanly on all four sides.
Top-to-bottom and side-to-side — or a seam shows at every repeat.
2 · Set the motif on an angle.
It hides the grid better than a square layout.
3 · Keep small type out of the tile.
Half of it will end up folded under or trimmed off.
4 · Keep the logo off the dead centre.
“The packer, not the designer, decides where the fold lands” —
margin discipline beats a centred layout.
5 · Space the repeat generously.
“A tight, busy repeat looks cheap up close, while a confident,
well-spaced motif feels considered.”
6 · Resist dating the art.
A pattern with a year has one window; a timeless pattern reorders.
Before the full run, order the trial quantity first — a pattern that tiles perfectly on screen can surprise on kraft. (4over4 artwork guidance, as published.)
